Periodic-compaction preferred phase: catch-up after an anchor

Real DBs (1000 per scenario per variant), periodic_compaction_seconds N=100s, real periodic-task scheduler, per-DB listeners recording every compaction. Each (scenario, variant) ran in its own process; DB IDs (hence preferred phases) are identical across variants, so differences come from the TriggerTime change plus timing noise. current (replicate) is a second run of the current code with the same phases: the gap between it and current is a noise reference.

1. Timeline — compactions per DB (an evenly spaced sample of DBs; colored = periodic, gray = write), selected variant

2. Periodic compaction load per DB per period (bins of period/40), all variants

3. Load around the change (bins of period/100), all variants

4. Badness over time, all variants

Cumulative (thick) and instantaneous (thin). Instantaneous is noisy; compare cumulative and the summary table.

Summary (side by side)

peak load = max periodic compactions per DB per period in period/40 bins after the change (from 0 when there is no change); 1.0 = perfectly even. early = average load over the first 0.1 period after the change. badness peak / steady / end as in the original page. Red = more than 5% worse than current (peak load or steady badness).
